label: mid-prefix first occurrence of r/2/k/o/d/c/h-type token after a b/g/e/q-type token
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase. It is never active at t=0, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. Activity peaks at positions 3-5 (2-6 hold about 98% of mass). It fires on the first occurrence of an input token, with in_first carrying 91% of mass. The current token matters: r, 2 and k are strongest (4x lift), then o, d, c, h, i, n, l, a and v. It is stronger when tokens such as b, g, e, q, z, 0, f, s, u or p appeared earlier in the prefix (first_tok in b/g/e/q gives 2.4x lift). The top activations are sequences that start with b/g/e/q and then input o, r, 2 or k at t=3-5. The unit behaves like a graded, roughly additive token-set code rather than a crisp rule. The predicate captures about 83% of activation mass at under 50% precision, so many matching steps stay below threshold. It does not fire on repeated tokens or on any step at or after <DEL>.
